source: NASA OSDR RadLab, plus published dose-equivalent values where RadLab has none
method: Per detector and UTC day: mean dose rate × 24 h ÷ 1000 (μGy/h → mGy/day; μSv/h → mSv/day). Detector-days with < 90% of that detector's busiest-day sample count are dropped; detectors are averaged per day. mGy_per_day is the mean of the days, typical_mGy_per_day (= median_mGy_per_day) their median, max_daily_mGy the highest day. notable_event flags consecutive days above 1.5 × the median. mSv_per_day is RadLab dose_equivalent_rate where it exists (basis "measured"), otherwise a value copied from a peer-reviewed paper (basis "published"). Cosmic Shield never applies a quality factor. 4 significant figures.
caveat: Absorbed dose (mGy) is measured in each instrument's detector material and is not dose equivalent (mSv). Measured and published mSv values come from different instruments, years and solar conditions than the absorbed-dose windows.
not_available: MSL-RAD cruise data (Dec 2011 - Aug 2012) is not in RadLab, so Mars transit has no absorbed dose.
IV-TEPC and TEPC are in RadLab (2014-2020) but their dose_equivalent_rate is empty, so ISS mSv/day comes from ALTEA-Survey.
No dose equivalent for lunar orbit (CRaTER reports absorbed dose only).
